operations.name: Kelly Postal

expected.charges: Minnesota state embezzlement prosecution concerning the Local 544 treasury following the union’s transfer to the CIO; separate from the Smith Act trial.
expected.convicted: Convicted in the separate state case.
expected.sentence: Five years imposed; historical account documents nine months actually served.

operations.source: https://www.themilitant.com/1945/0903/MIL0903.pdf — The Militant, January 20, 1945, page 1, obituary of Mae Postal, explicitly reports Kelly Postal released on parole May 30, 1944, on condition of moving to Oregon. Applies to state embezzlement imprisonment, not the separate federal acquittal. Admission day remains unknown; no date calculated from nine months.

operations.name: Dan Schwankl

expected.charges: Federal trespass during the 2004 School of the Americas Watch vigil at Fort Benning, Georgia
expected.sentence: 90 days in federal prison and a $500 fine. Source: https://www.soaw-austin.org/POC1983_2012.php

operations.source: https://media.nukeresister.org/wp-content/uploads/resister/nr137.pdf — The Nuclear Resister #137, July 29, 2005, printed page 3, SOA Grads’ Abuses Fuel Resistance, explicitly names Dan Schwankl among nine who began serving on March 15. Original PDF retrieved from publisher’s relocated media host, text extracted and page visually checked. Existing June 10 release preserved; admission is not back-calculated from sentence.

operations.name: José Víctor García Díaz

expected.charges: Civil immigration detention; plaintiff alleging retaliation for farmworker organizing.

updates.sentence: Civil immigration detention pending removal; released on $1,500 bond. This was administrative detention, not a criminal prison sentence.

operations.source: https://socialistworker.org/2016/05/09/detained-for-organizing-vermont-workers — May 9, 2016 retrospective explicitly says Victor Diaz was released on bail May 4. https://vtdigger.org/2016/05/04/migrant-justice-group-bail-granted-for-activist-facing-deportation/ contemporaneously confirms May 4 grant of $1,500 bail, but describes release prospectively; the later report establishes actual release. Identity matched to full Jose Victor Garcia-Diaz name, Migrant Justice and April 21 detention. No end to removal proceedings or supervision inferred.

operations.name: Tandre Buchanan

expected.charges: Hobbs Act robbery of a Cleveland shop during May 30 2020 unrest

updates.prosecutor: Assistant United States Attorney Scott C. Zarzycki
updates.convicted: Yes — jury verdict on Hobbs Act robbery and aiding and abetting, and tampering with evidence.

operations.source: https://www.justice.gov/usao-ndoh/pr/cleveland-man-sentenced-prison-after-robbery-and-evidence-tampering-conviction — March 23, 2022 DOJ report establishes sentence date, judge and trial prosecutor. https://law.justia.com/cases/federal/appellate-courts/ca6/22-3697/22-3697-2023-08-21.html — Sixth Circuit opinion establishes July 23, 2020 indictment and jury convictions. Conflict: opinion dates arrest June 10, while populated database field says June 11. Existing arrest left unchanged; no uninterrupted incarceration dates assigned. Restitution was partially vacated, so no restitution amount added.
